messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: Sort boxplot by medians
parts:
Hi Rists, I can't seem to find a simple way of sorting the boxes in a
boxplot by their respective medians. I'm trying to order the boxes by
local speaking rate rather than informant ID number, which is what I
get with:

boxplot(data$LOC.SPK.RATE~data$INF)

I know you can do so manually by first sorting the medians with
tapply, such as in

sort(tapply(data$LOC.SPK.RATE, data$INF, median))

and then manually writing the ordered informant ID numbers in the
code, as in:

boxplot(
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==3],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==1],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==4],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==6],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==7],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==5],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==8],
data$LOC.SPK.RATE[data$INF==2])

but I assume there's a quicker way. I didn't see an argument of
boxplot in the documentation (?boxplot) that seems to sort by median.
Am I missing it? It seems like this would be a useful argument.
Writing the code manually doesn't take too long with only eight
informants, but it could quickly become cumbersome as the number of
informants increases.

Thanks in advance for your help. Earl Brown

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Sort boxplot by medians
parts:
like this?

# random number seed
set.seed(1)

NUM <- rnorm(100) # some numbers
FAC <-factor(rep(letters[1:5], 20)) # some factor
boxplot(NUM~FAC, notch=TRUE) # not so nice plot

oi <- order(tapply(NUM, FAC, median)) # create order index
FAC <- factor(FAC, levels=levels(FAC)[oi]) # apply it
boxplot(NUM~FAC, notch=TRUE) # better plot


STG

messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: Re: Sort boxplot by medians
parts:
Yes, that worked, with a little tweaking. I had to create a new factor
in the data frame. When I tried to overwrite the factor with:

data$INFORMANT<-factor(data$INFORMANT, ...)[oi]

it just gave me <NA> when I look at the individual tokens (when I
typed "data$INFORMANT" at the console). So, I created a new factor:

data$INFORMANT.ORDERED<-factor(data$INFORMANT, ...)[oi]

and it worked. Thanks again.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Sort boxplot by medians
parts:
You are trying to use a string (that you paste together) as if it was
a proper function and not a string, which you can't do. But why not do
the much simpler?
for (i in 1:6) {

boxplot(some.data.frame[,i])
}

Or even better, without a loop:

data(iris)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
sapply(iris[,1:4], boxplot, notch=TRUE)
par(mfrow=c(1,1))

Cf. Ch. 5 in SLFWR.

STG

I would use data$Examen[,i] to access all the data in a column. The following produces 6 simple boxplots in a 2 x 3 display:

> data <- matrix(1:60, nrow = 10)
> par(mfrow=c(2,3))
> for (i in 1:6) {

+ boxplot(data[,i])
+ }

And just for the sake of completeness: if in this example (for no good
reason ;-)) you want to paste together a string and use that string as
a function, do it with eval(parse(text=...)):

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
for (i in 1:4) {
boxplot(eval(parse(text=paste("iris[,", i, "]", sep=""))), notch=TRUE)

}

are labeled "Examen.1", "Examen.2", etc. and not just "1", "2", I used

proposed:

column<-grep(paste("Examen.", i, sep=""), names(data), perl=T)

boxplot(data[,column])

}

I couldn't get the sapply solution to work. Here's what I tried:

but the loop solution works.

Thanks again. I appreciate everyone's help. I'm continually amazed by
what R can do. Earl Brown
